end.summary:
Identified litter, plastic, plant damage, scratched walls, noise, feeding animals, and coral damage as harms to special places.
Suggested carrying rubbish away, staying on paths, and not touching coral or feeding animals.
Explained how repeated small actions by many visitors can create large harm.
Explained that grass roots hold soil and that removing grass can cause erosion.
Feeding wild animals as helpful remained a mix-up at the end; the small-wrapper idea was corrected later.
end.parentNote: Asha practised ways visitors can protect fragile places and used examples such as coral, bats, monkeys, grass, and litter. Tara explained several cause-and-effect links, including how grass roots hold soil and how many small actions add up. Tara corrected the idea that one wrapper does not matter, but still needed a reminder that feeding wild animals can harm their diet and behaviour. At home, discuss one local place and make a short “protect it” list, including carrying rubbish home and not feeding animals.
